summary: Office printer network flapping on 3rd floor - intermittent DNS failures
description:
Issue summary: Third-floor shared printers (two devices: HP-LaserJet-3A and Brother-MFC-3B) intermittently drop from the office network and DNS. This causes print jobs to queue and fail, impacting ~10-15 users in that zone.

Impact: Blocks printing for small teams and interferes with on-site demos and hardware sign-off. Not affecting production services, but causing recurring user support tickets.

Environment: On-prem office LAN, Cisco switch stack on floor 3, DHCP+internal DNS, VLAN 20 (office), static IP assignment via DHCP reservation for printers.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Print job submitted from Mac or Windows workstation on VLAN 20.
2) Job queues for several minutes, then fails with "printer unreachable".
3) Devices show as offline in the printer UI and respond to pings intermittently.
4) After 2–10 minutes device returns to network and queued jobs print.

Recent logs and observations:
- Switch logs (03/12-03/16) show short flaps on ports 3/21 and 3/22 correlating to HP-LaserJet-3A and Brother-MFC-3B (link-state flaps 10–30s).
- DHCP server logs show lease renewals around same timestamps.
- DNS entries briefly fail to resolve to the reserved IP, client fallbacks attempt direct IP which also times out.
- No power cycling observed in camera footage; both devices have latest vendor firmware (checked 2026-02).

Attempts so far:
- Rebooted printers and switch stack (03/11 restart) — temporary improvement for ~24 hours.
- Replaced patch cables for both printers (03/13).
- Confirmed firmware up to date and vendor known issues check (no known matching bug).
- Scoped DHCP lease durations; increased lease TTL to 24h as test (no effect).

Hypothesis: Intermittent link flapping likely due to switch port or SFP module; could be temperature-related or power-supply hiccup on switch. Alternate hypothesis is ARP/DNS cache misbehavior on the DHCP/DNS server causing short resolution outages.

Next steps / proposed remediation:
- Swap the switch SFP/module for stack member A to isolate hardware (owner: Networking).
- Move printers temporarily to spare ports on different switch member and monitor for 72 hours.
- Enable enhanced debug logging on DHCP/DNS server for VLAN 20 for another 48h.
- If hardware swap doesn't resolve, schedule vendor support ticket with switch vendor and open SUP ticket for DHCP/DNS investigation.

Owner / point of contact: Elena Martinez (Facilities/IT); please coordinate with Networking (A. Chen) and Office Ops (M. Lopez).
